themes_detail.label: Bike Lane & Park Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about bike/roller/skate activity and park rule violations have spiked dramatically this week and last week — 3 bike complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score 8.69) and 4 park violations 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score 8.66) — suggesting either new enforcement activity, a sudden behavioral shift, or both in St. George's parks and streets.
evidence: Bike/Roller/Skate complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Park rule violations: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
Both complaints show highest z-scores in dataset, indicating statistical extremity
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about enforcement changes or new park programs in St. George
Talk to residents about what triggered complaints — new skateboard park use, enforcement crackdown, or community organizing?

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Disappearing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints tripled this week alone — 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (243% spike, z-score 3.54) — indicating either recent vandalism, deterioration, or a sign replacement/installation backlog in the district.
evidence: Missing street sign complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% spike, z-score 3.54)
This is the most recent spike in the dataset (occurred this week, not 2-3 weeks ago)
Aligns with long-standing community board budget request for street light repair — suggests wider infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Request DOT data on street sign replacement schedules and maintenance backlog in CD 501
Canvass affected blocks to identify if vandalism or weathering is the root cause

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Dead Trees Escalating
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying trees have spiked sharply over the past 2-3 weeks — 11 complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (319% increase, z-score 3.58) — and illegal tree damage complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 5 vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% increase, z-score 4.96), suggesting environmental stress, storm damage, or lack of tree maintenance in the district.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 11 last week vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (319% spike, z-score 3.58)
Illegal Tree Damage complaints: 5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% spike, z-score 4.96)
Two converging environmental signals suggest systemic issue — either weather event, disease, or deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department about tree health assessments and recent storm/weather impacts in St. George
Interview residents on specific blocks with dead trees to understand maintenance complaints and timeline

themes_detail.label: Lot Deterioration & Vacant Property Problem
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked to 5 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (1233% increase, z-score 6.65) — a sharp spike suggesting either increased complaints about abandoned or deteriorating lots, or a concentrated problem area emerging in the district.
evidence: Lot Condition complaints: 5 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% spike, z-score 6.65)
Converges with long-standing community board request to address illegal conversions and building misuse (DOB jurisdiction)
May relate to 626 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days — unclear if alteration permits are addressing or creating neglect
reporting_angles: Map the 5 lot condition complaints to identify if they cluster in one neighborhood area or are dispersed
Cross-reference with DOB violations and ULURP applications (3 non-ULURP and 1 ULURP active) to see if development pipeline is leaving lots vacant

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, Cabs) jumped to 6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (269% increase, z-score 3.94) — indicating growing friction around rideshare congestion, illegal pickups, or driver behavior in the district.
evidence: For-Hire Vehicle complaints: 6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score 3.94)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago but has not receded, suggesting sustained concern rather than one-off event
No Reddit or local news coverage yet — potential untold story on gig economy impacts in outer boroughs
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners about specific complaints — illegal pickups, traffic obstruction, safety concerns?
Check if new transit hubs, development projects, or ferry terminal activity have triggered rideshare clustering
